# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Age:** Over fifty years old  <sub>[v1 c26 P15](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c26 P1](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper for college students  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c34 P13](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0013)</sub>
- **Titles:** Aunt Euphemia  <sub>[v1 c26 P11](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0011)</sub>; Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v2 c4 P12](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0012)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a small, elderly woman with a gentle, triangular face, rosy cheeks, and irrepressible, youthful blue eyes. Her silver-white hair is arranged in charming small rolls above her ears. She dresses in outmoded clothes, including a green gingham apron when working.

_Sources: [v1 c30 P0](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0000)_

## Personality

Aunt Euphemia is an extremely independent, cheerful, and indulgent woman who possesses a young, buoyant spirit despite her age. She refuses to supervise or strictly control the young women in her care, preferring a relaxed lifestyle where everyone can enjoy themselves. Unbothered by small domestic mishaps, she meets life's troubles with humor, common sense, and warm hospitality.

_Sources: [v1 c27 P0](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0000), [v1 c34 P15](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0015), [v1 c35 P16](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0016), [v1 c37 P24](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0024)_

## Traits

- Indulgent and easygoing  <sub>[v1 c37 P24](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0024)</sub>
- Humorous and cheerful  <sub>[v1 c35 P16](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0016)</sub>
- Possesses practical common sense  <sub>[v1 c37 P24](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0024)</sub>
- Fear of snakes  <sub>[v1 c34 P16](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0016)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting and fine needlework  <sub>[v1 c35 P15](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0015)</sub>
- Domestic management and cooking  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c35 P16](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0016)</sub>

## Goals

- Live comfortably and relax in her older years
- Provide a warm, welcoming home for Mabel, Nell, Honora, and Cressy  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c34 P13](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0013)</sub>

## History

Aunt Euphemia's father died at sea shortly before her birth, leading to her being named Jamesina, though she went by Euphemia. She grew up in a family with six daughters and later married, though her husband passed away, as did her only daughter's departure for missionary work in India. Left alone in a large house, she agreed to move to Portmaris to keep house for her niece Mabel Colby and her friends Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay at Tabby's Place. She quickly became a beloved, reassuring presence in their lives, accommodating their friends and pets, including three cats. She managed the household for two academic years, providing the young women with a home-like environment. When the girls graduated from Wexcombe College, she decided to remain at Tabby's Place to care for her cats and the house rather than travel.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c27 P41](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0041), [v1 c34 P13](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0013), [v1 c34 P16](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0016), [v1 c35 P0](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0000), [v1 c37 P24](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0024)_

## Background by volume

- Given the official name Jamesina after her deceased father, James, but called Euphemia or Phemie  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013)</sub>
- Her only daughter married and left for a foreign mission field in India  <sub>[v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c34 P16](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0016)</sub>
- Raised in a family with around six daughters  <sub>[v1 c27 P41](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0041)</sub>
